newsitem.title: UK: UK gas interruptions down as milder weather return.
newsitem.headline: UK gas interruptions down as milder weather return.

text.p: TransCo, the pipeline and distribution division of British Gas plc, said on Monday that gas supplies are only being interrupted to holders of interruptible contracts in two of Britain's 13 Local Distribution Zones (LDZs) in the current gas day.
A spokeswoman for TransCo said that the whole of the South West LDZ was currently facing interruption, as is 70 percent of the South Wales LDZ.
She added that a "small amount" of Network Sensitive Load was being interrupted nationwide. The gas day lasts 24 hours from 06.00 GMT.
This level of interruption compares with Thursday and Friday of last week, when all interruptible contracts in southern Britain were cut.

Customers with interruptible contracts pay less for gas than holders of "firm" contracts which guarantee supply. But they must be prepared to stop using gas and switch to alternative fuels, such as fuel oil, when demand peaks occur, so as to ensure security of supply to other users.

There had been fears that demand would surge on Monday, as business and industry return to full capacity after the extended Christmas break. Electricity demand, some of which is powered by natural gas, was forecast on Sunday evening at 49,753 MegaWatts (mW) for the half hour ending at 17.30 GMT on Monday. This would have been a record.

But by Monday morning, as it became clear the weather was milder than had been expected, the National Grid had revised this down to "in excess of" 48,000 mW, below the record of 48,811 set last January. Milder weather is also responsible for TransCo suspending the interruptions called at the end of last week.
